stem.en: Scientists described the purple frog in 2003. Why does this not mean that its family began in 2003?

text.en: It dates the description, and fossils show an older family.

feedback.en: Right. A discovery date is a fact about what people know, not about the age of the family.

text.en: Scientists cannot be sure of the year in which any species was described.

feedback.en: The year is known. The fault lies in reading it as the age of the family.

text.en: The purple frog is known only from fossils, so it has no living members.

feedback.en: The purple frog is a living animal. It breeds during the monsoon.

text.en: Every family of living things began within the last few hundred years.

feedback.en: Fossils show that many families are far older than that.

explanation.en: The year 2003 records a change in what people know. The age of the family comes from other evidence, such as fossils.

hints.en: Ask what changed in 2003: the frog, or what people knew about it?
